description:
FILED s473d (Opus, 2026-09-07) while fixing #1012 (the %.15g style switch).
PRE-EXISTING in shape -- the same divergence already applied above 1e16 before
this session -- and now UNIFORM across every decade, which is the reason it is
filed rather than left as a decade-shaped accident.

MEASURED, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on the s473d tree (scratch/s473d/s3.pl):

    expression                perl                     PCL
    1e15                      1e+15                    1e+15      agree
    1000000000000000.0        1e+15                    1e+15      agree
    1e15 + 0.5                1e+15                    1e+15      agree
    sqrt(1e30)                1e+15                    1e+15      agree
    1000000000000000          1000000000000000         same       agree
    1000000 * 1000000000      1000000000000000         same       agree
    1e14 * 10                 1000000000000000  (IV)   1e+15      DIVERGE
    -1 * 1e15                 -1000000000000000 (IV)   -1e+15     DIVERGE
    1e15 + 1                  1000000000000001  (IV)   1e+15      DIVERGE
    1e15 * 10                 10000000000000000 (IV)   1e+16      DIVERGE (already did)

THE MECHANISM.  perl's pp_multiply / pp_add preserve IV-ness: when both
operands can be read as IVs (and an INTEGRAL NV can -- SvIV_please succeeds on
1e14) and the product fits, the result SV is IOK and `sv_2pv` prints its
digits.  A float LITERAL is NOK-only and goes through Gconvert's %.15g.  PCL's
scalar has no IOK/NOK pair: a double stays a double, so both spellings print
through the %.15g rule.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT TRADE TODAY, not a regression to undo.  Before s473d the
%.15g branch was chosen from `(floor (log v 10d0))`, which is 14 for exactly
1e15, so PCL printed 1000000000000000 for BOTH spellings -- right for the
arithmetic one and wrong for the literal one, in the ONE decade [1e15,1e16).
Above 1e16 PCL already printed the exponential form for both, i.e. already
diverged on the arithmetic spelling.  Fixing #1012 makes the rule uniform and
moves the divergence, it does not create it: measured over the 12 shapes above
the score is 8 agree / 4 diverge BEFORE and 8 agree / 4 diverge AFTER, with
`1e15`, `1000000000000000.0`, `1e15+0.5` and `sqrt(1e30)` moving INTO
agreement and `1e14*10`, `-1*1e15`, `1e15+1` out of it.  The full perl-tests
sweep and the op/ companion leg are the bar and both were clean.

WHAT IMPLEMENTING IT WOULD TAKE: an IOK/NOK pair on the scalar (or an
"integral-double that came from IV arithmetic" tag), plus IV preservation in
pp_multiply/pp_add/pp_subtract's PCL equivalents.  That is the same
number-representation change task #1513 costed and the USER ruled DOCUMENTED
rather than implemented (2026-09-07), so this belongs to that ruling: see
`docs/not-supported.md` section "Integers are unbounded: PCL has no 64-bit
boundary", where the table above is now the section's fourth face.

DO NOT "fix" it by widening the %.15g threshold back to 1e16 -- that only
moves the same trade one decade up and abandons the rule perl actually
implements (`docs/ir-spec.md` section 3.2).

Guard rows: `Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t` D2 asserts all eight shapes, so an
implementation of IV preservation trips it deliberately.
subject: An integral ARITHMETIC result is an IV in perl and prints its digits, while the same value as a float literal is an NV and prints through %.15g -- PCL has one representation, so `1e14 * 10` prints 1e+15
